subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable auto-cleanup and archival policy for webhook/hook sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit hook-session cleanup policy, and what defaults and transcript-retention behavior should it use alongside `session.maintenance`, `cron.sessionRetention`, and persistent hook-session reuse?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the public config API, default cleanup behavior, transcript deletion or archival semantics, and interaction with reusable hook sessions are product and data-retention choices.

options.title: Add explicit hook cleanup policy
options.body: Introduce a default-safe `hooks.sessionCleanup` style policy with on-complete, delayed, and never modes plus transcript-retention behavior and focused hook/session tests.

options.title: Rely on generic maintenance
options.body: Document that hook sessions are governed only by `session.maintenance` age, count, and disk controls, and close hook-specific cleanup as not planned.

options.title: Defer until persistent mode is settled
options.body: Pause cleanup policy until persistent hook-session semantics are finalized so reuse and cleanup are designed together.

recommendation.title: Add explicit hook cleanup policy
recommendation.body: Introduce a default-safe `hooks.sessionCleanup` style policy with on-complete, delayed, and never modes plus transcript-retention behavior and focused hook/session tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter supplied the prior product-direction review for this issue and is the strongest routing signal from discussion plus current path history.
